content: The efficiency of bowser delivery lies in its ability to significantly reduce non-productive time, ensuring that equipment remains operational and project timelines are adhered to. Scalability is achieved by adjusting the frequency of deliveries and the size of the bowser fleet to match the fluctuating fuel demands of the project lifecycle. While explicit data on recent advancements in bowser-specific delivery logistics remains somewhat limited, the broader context of logistics and delivery infrastructure provides valuable insights into its potential. For instance, the rapid growth of the quick commerce sector in South Africa, which is projected to reach USD 130.7 billion, indicates a robust and expanding logistical framework capable of supporting specialized delivery operations, including bulk liquids and fuels [1] . Furthermore, the general growth in delivery ecosystems, supported by policy-driven logistical improvements and operational reforms, suggests a highly favorable environment for the expansion and optimization of mobile fuel delivery services like bowser operations [3] [14] . Competitors leveraging bowser delivery are increasingly focusing on integrating routing software and real-time tracking to enhance the efficiency of their fleets, thereby adapting to broader market developments and ensuring reliable supply chains even in remote mining and construction locations [1] . In contrast to the highly mobile nature of bowser delivery, the deployment of on-site storage tanks offers a stationary but highly reliable service model for bulk diesel supply. This model involves the installation of high-capacity fuel storage units directly at the mining or construction site, providing a continuous and readily accessible reservoir of diesel. Fuel management systems represent the most technologically advanced service model within the competitor landscape, seamlessly integrating hardware and software to provide comprehensive oversight of diesel consumption and inventory. These systems are designed to track fuel usage down to the individual piece of equipment or operator, generating actionable data that can be used to identify inefficiencies, prevent fuel theft, and optimize overall fuel economy. In the context of mining and construction, where fuel constitutes a significant portion of operating expenses, the implementation of sophisticated fuel management systems offers unparalleled efficiency.
